questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Mr. Johnson teaches us mathematics.

options.text: Mathematics was taught to us by Mr. Johnson.
Mathematics is being taught to us by Mr. Johnson.
Mathematics is taught to us by Mr. Johnson.
Mathematics will be taught to us by Mr. Johnson.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **active voice: **"Mr. Johnson teaches us mathematics."
 
• To convert it into passive voice, the object of the active sentence **("mathematics")** becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The correct structure for the passive voice sentence is: **"Mathematics is taught to us by Mr. Johnson."**
 
• Option 3 correctly follows this structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Mathematics** is taught **to us by Mr. Johnson."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Mathematics was taught to us by Mr. Johnson." - This is in the past tense, which is incorrect.
 
• **Option 2:** "Mathematics is being taught to us by Mr. Johnson." - This indicates an ongoing action, which is incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "Mathematics will be taught to us by Mr. Johnson." - This is in the future tense, which is incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

“Hurrah! I have topped again,” he said. “Congratulations,” said I.

options.text: He exclaimed that he topped, and I congratulated him.
He said that he topped again. I congratulated him
He exclaimed with joy that he had topped again. I congratulated him.
He said to me he had topped again, and I congratulated him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, exclamatory sentences are often transformed using words like** "exclaimed," "with joy," or "with sorrow," as appropriate to convey the emotion.**
 
• The verb **"said" **is often replaced with "exclaimed" to reflect the exclamatory nature of the statement.
 
• In indirect speech, the present perfect tense "have topped" is usually changed to the past perfect tense** "had topped."**
 
• The phrase **"Hurrah!" **is a joyful exclamation and should be conveyed with equivalent emotional intensity in the indirect speech form.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

Correct Sentence: ***He exclaimed with joy that he had topped again. I congratulated him**.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The phrase "He exclaimed that he topped" does not convey the correct tense or emotional intensity.
 
• **Option 2:** The phrase "He said that he topped again" fails to capture the exclamatory nature and the correct tense.
 
• **Option 4:** The phrase "He said to me he had topped again" misses the emotional context provided by "exclaimed."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Who is looking for a smart advisor?

options.text: By whom is a smart advisor looked?
By whom was a smart advisor looked?
By whom is a smart advisor looked for?
By whom is a smart advisor being looked for?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence in active voice is **"Who is looking for a smart advisor?"**
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the** passive sentence.**
 
• The correct passive construction includes the use of **"by"** to indicate the doer and the appropriate form of the verb **"to be"** with the past participle.
 
• The correct transformation is **"By whom is a smart advisor being looked for?"**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The teacher orders Mohan not to tear off pages from his note-book.

options.text: The teacher says to Mohan, “Let the pages not be torn off from your notebook.”
The teacher says to Mohan, “You shouldn’t tear off pages from your notebook.”
The teacher says to Mohan, “Don’t tear off pages from your notebook.”
The teacher says to Mohan, “Mustn’t tear off pages from your notebook.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by someone, using **quotation marks.**
 
• In the given options, only Option 3 correctly uses **direct speech format.**
 
• Option 3 states: ***"The teacher says to Mohan, 'Don’t tear off pages from your notebook.'"***
 
• This sentence accurately represents the teacher's order in **direct speech.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

Correct Sentence: ***"The teacher says to Mohan, 'Don’t tear off pages from your notebook.'"***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Let the pages not be torn off from your notebook." - This is not a common way to give a direct order in English.
 
• **Option 2:** "You shouldn’t tear off pages from your notebook." - This is a suggestion rather than a direct order.
 
• **Option 4:** "Mustn’t tear off pages from your notebook." - This is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) fell dead in an instant

(B) stunned the movement

(C) of the busy Bazaar and

(D) silenced the cacophony

(E) suddenly, a ringing blast

(F) out of the bodies, which
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence begins with part (E),** "suddenly, a ringing blast," which sets the scene for the sudden event.**
 
• Next is part (D),** "silenced the cacophony,"** explaining the immediate effect of the blast.
 
• Following this is part (C), "of the busy Bazaar and," providing more detail about what exactly was silenced.
 
• Then comes part (B),** "stunned the movement,"** describing the additional impact of the blast.
 
• Subsequently, part (F), **"out of the bodies, which," **transitions to the result of the stunned movement.
 
• Finally, part (A) completes the sentence with **"fell dead in an instant."**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate title for the passage.

options.text: Herbal Remedies: A Way of Life

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Explanation:** The passage repeatedly emphasizes the potential dangers of herbal remedies and the importance of caution, making "Risks with Herbal Remedies" the most fitting title.
 
• **The Benefits of Herbal Concoctions:** This title is misleading as the passage does not primarily focus on benefits, but rather on the necessity of careful use and awareness of risks.
 
• **Herbal Remedies:** This title is too broad and does not encapsulate the cautionary advice given in the passage.
 
• **Herbal Remedies: A Way of Life:** This title suggests an endorsement or positive viewpoint, which is contrary to the passage's warning and advice to not substitute traditional medicine with herbal remedies.
 
• In **summary**, the title in **option 3**, "Risks with Herbal Remedies," accurately reflects the main idea and tone of the passage, which emphasizes caution and the potential dangers of using herbal concoctions.

questions.question: Identify the statement that holds true according to the passage.

options.text: Herbal concoctions should not be used for curing minor illnesses.
Herbal remedies can sometimes contain artificial ingredients.
Herbal remedies can be trusted blindly.
Herbal remedies have no proven health benefits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Explanation:** The passage mentions that not all herbal concoctions are natural and organic and that some may contain synthetic ingredients or preservatives, making this statement true.
 
• **Herbal concoctions should not be used for curing minor illnesses:** The passage states that some herbs may be used for minor ailments such as a cold or headache, making this statement incorrect.
 
• **Herbal remedies can be trusted blindly:** The passage advises caution and the need for research and consultation with healthcare professionals before using any herbal concoction, indicating that herbal remedies should not be trusted blindly.
 
• **Herbal remedies have no proven health benefits:** The passage acknowledges that some herbal remedies may have proven health benefits, making this statement incorrect.
 
• In **summary**, the statement in **option 2**, **"Herbal remedies can sometimes contain artificial ingredients," **is true according to the passage, which highlights the necessity of reading labels and researching herbal concoctions before use.

questions.question: Select the option that best describes the central theme of the passage.

options.text: While herbal remedies may have some benefits, these should be used cautiously and in consultation with health professionals.
Herbal remedies can cause cancer and heart disease.
Herbal remedies are essential for fighting all sorts of modern diseases
Herbal remedies can successfully replace all other forms of medication.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Options 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Explanation:** The passage** emphasizes **both the potential benefits and the risks of using herbal remedies. It highlights the importance of researching and consulting with healthcare professionals before using herbal concoctions, underscoring the necessity of caution.
 
• **Herbal remedies can cause cancer and heart disease:** The passage suggests that some herbal remedies may treat serious conditions, but it does not explicitly state that herbal remedies can cause these diseases. This option is misleading.
 
• **Herbal remedies are essential for fighting all sorts of modern diseases:** The passage does not make a sweeping endorsement of herbal remedies as essential for fighting modern diseases. Instead, it advises cautious and informed use.
 
• **Herbal remedies can successfully replace all other forms of medication:** The passage explicitly advises against using herbal remedies as a substitute for traditional medicine, making this option incorrect.
 
• In **summary**, option **1** most accurately captures the central theme of the passage. It reflects the balance between acknowledging the potential benefits of herbal remedies and stressing the importance of caution and professional consultation.

Substitute
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of the passage, the word "**substitute**" refers to something used in place of another.
 
• The antonym of "**substitute**" would be something that matches in function or form and is not a replacement.
 
• "**Equivalent**" means something that is equal in value, amount, function, meaning, etc., but not a substitute.
 
• Thus, the antonym of "substitute" in this context is "**equivalent**".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Perdurable**: enduring continuously; imperishable. This does not serve as an antonym for "substitute".
 
• **Rival**: a person or thing competing with another. This does not serve as an antonym for "substitute".
 
• **Surrogate**: a substitute, especially a person deputizing for another. This is more of a synonym than an antonym.
